title: Arkret Moderation Appeal
description: Payload shapes for the four ak.moderation.appeal.* event kinds (submit / review / decision / close) that close the moderation appeal loop. Each kind writes the ak.component.moderation.appeal.v1 cell on a deterministic state machine: (none) → submitted → under_review → decided → closed; close from submitted/under_review is allowed only for appellant withdrawal (closer == appellant and close_reason=appellant_withdrawn). The decided state additionally records the verdict (uphold / overturn / modify); overturn MUST be paired in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction with a ak.moderation.decision.lift event referencing the original decision. Modify MUST atomically lift the original decision and add the replacement decision named by modify_decision_ref. Lifting a decision does not resurrect an irreversible redaction tombstone or destroyed content key. All payloads carry realm_id and reducers MUST require it to equal the enclosing Event.realm_id and the appealed decision's Realm. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal strand). Capability: ak.moderation.appeal.submit (any member, low risk) for submit; ak.moderation.appeal.review (moderator) for review/decision/manual reviewer close after decided; appellant withdrawal is authorized by closer == appellant.

decision_ref.description: Reference to the ak.moderation.decision event being appealed.

target_ref.description: The original moderation target (message, strand, member, blob, etc.) — same typed-id form as the appealed decision's target.

evidence_visibility.description: Who may decrypt / read the appeal evidence narrative. Default per Realm policy; SHOULD be reviewers_only for sensitive disputes. The visibility tag MUST enter projection / redaction decisions; it does NOT change wire encryption of the envelope, only the plaintext audience for evidence fields.

submit_payload.description: ak.moderation.appeal.submit — opens the appeal. Writes appeal cell (state=submitted). MUST be issued by an appellant who is the original moderation target's controller (member appealing their own ban / message removal) or by an authorized advocate listed in Realm policy. A Realm member appellant is admitted by baseline membership; a non-member advocate MUST be authorized by Realm policy / ak.moderation.appeal.submit capability.

appellant.description: Actor lodging the appeal. MUST be the original moderation target's controller or an authorized advocate.

reason_text_ref.description: Reference (typically blob_ref or in-line short string) to the appeal narrative / supporting argument. For E2EE Realms this is an encrypted reference.

evidence_refs.description: Optional supporting evidence (blob refs, prior message ids, witness DIDs).

review_payload.description: ak.moderation.appeal.review — reviewer takes the appeal under review. Transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Reviewer MUST hold ak.moderation.appeal.review capability; the same actor MUST NOT review their own moderation decision (separation of duties enforced by reducer).

decision_payload.description: ak.moderation.appeal.decision — reviewer's verdict. Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Verdict semantics: uphold = original decision stands, no further action; overturn = original decision is lifted for future governance evaluation, this event MUST be paired in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction with a ak.moderation.decision.lift event whose target equals decision_ref (reducer rejects with appeal_overturn_missing_lift otherwise), and irreversible redaction/key-destruction effects are not resurrected; modify = original decision is atomically replaced, requiring both a same-batch lift of decision_ref and a new ak.moderation.decision whose event id is modify_decision_ref.

reason_text_ref.description: Reference to the verdict rationale. MUST be present for audit trail; visibility follows evidence_visibility on the submit event.

modify_decision_ref.description: Required iff verdict=modify. Points to the replacement ak.moderation.decision event in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction; that transaction MUST also contain a ak.moderation.decision.lift for the original appealed decision.

close_payload.description: ak.moderation.appeal.close — closes the appeal from decided, or from submitted/under_review only for appellant withdrawal. Reviewer close and a deployment's authorized close service use the review capability after the appeal is decided; appellant withdrawal is authorized by closer == appellant plus close_reason=appellant_withdrawn while state is submitted or under_review. close is a manual/authorized action: the protocol does not mandate any auto-close timer, timeout duration, or cool-off duration — deployment/Realm policy decides those. Idempotency only: the same (decision_ref, appellant) pair MUST NOT have two non-closed appeals concurrently; a fresh appeal_id is allowed once the prior appeal cell is closed.

closer.description: Actor or service closing the appeal (reviewer, appellant, or a deployment's authorized close service). Reducer authorizes the close via the normal capability gate (or closer == appellant for withdrawal); the protocol does not mandate any timer service DID or timeout window.

auto_closed.description: Informational marker: true iff the close was emitted by a deployment's automated close service rather than a human actor. The protocol attaches no special timer/window enforcement to this flag; deployment policy defines when (if ever) automated close fires.

close_reason.description: Machine-readable close cause. appellant_withdrawn is valid only when closer is the appellant and the appeal is still submitted or under_review; timer_expired is an optional label for a deployment's automated close (auto_closed=true) and carries no protocol-mandated timeout semantics.
